subject: Follow-up: Flux Health demo — proposed POC & success map
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@fluxhealth.com>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@fluxhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Flux Health demo — proposed POC & success map

Hi Samantha / Carlos — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and a concrete proposed POC so we can keep momentum.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Goal: reduce triage time for inbound clinical tickets by surfacing suggested actions and relevant documentation (target: 45% reduction in average time-to-first-action).
- Primary dataset: anonymized triage transcripts + EHR metadata (no PHI in the sample feed we reviewed).
- Success for Flux: precision of suggestions >= 70% on core triage intents, and safe handling of PHI in the ingestion pipeline.

Proposed POC (6 weeks) — high level:
Week 0: alignment & kickoff — confirm scope, stakeholders, network access, and data slice (1 day)
Week 1: onboarding & small pilot dataset ingestion (up to 50k tokens) — verify format and telemetry
Week 2-3: model tuning + evaluation on held-out set; run suggested prompts and acceptance metric collection
Week 4: integration testing with a small user group (5–8 agents) + latency/load check
Week 5: success metrics review; remediation on edge cases
Week 6: final readout + handoff and next-step commercial proposal

Owners:
- Flux Health: Samantha Ortiz (Product lead), Carlos Ruiz (Data / infra)
- Redwood: Priyom Das (AE / program owner), Ben Carter (SE), Marissa Cole (CSM)

Proposed success criteria (please confirm or modify):
1) Suggestion precision >= 70% across the core triage intents we defined in the call
2) Median response latency < 300ms for the UI call path
3) No PHI persisted in cleartext in any telemetry logs; proof-of-process for redaction/anonymization
4) Qualitative CSAT from pilot agents >= 4/5 on helpfulness

Attachments: poc-outline-fluxhealth.pdf (detailed week-by-week), sample-telemetry-schema.json

Ask: can you confirm the stakeholders above and whether the proposed 6-week window looks feasible? If yes, I’ll schedule a kickoff and share the access checklist. If you need procurement or security reviews first, let us know the timeline and we can shift.

Thanks,
Priyom

Thanks Priyom — this is helpful and aligns with our internal thinking. A few notes/questions: 

- Appreciate the clarity on owners. Please add Liam Grant (Security & Compliance) to the thread — he’ll need to sign off on the telemetry approach. (liam.grant@fluxhealth.com)
- On success criteria #3: we need an explicit PHI-safe ingest validation step in Week 1 (sample verification + automated redaction check). Can you add that as a must-have?
- Procurement: we’re good on budget but procurement has a calendar backlog. Can we target a kickoff the week of May 29 instead of next week? That pushes the end date by one week but gives us time to run the security questionnaire.

I’ve looped in Carlos who will be the technical point-of-contact for dataset access. Carlos — can you confirm whether you can provide a sanitized sample by May 24?

On the evaluation metrics, Flux would also like to include a short human review panel (3 clinicians) in Week 5 for qualitative feedback — can Redwood support scheduling and a short rubric?

Appreciate it,
Samantha

Quick technical notes from the SE side — thanks for the outline Priyom. A few risks and asks before kickoff: 

Risks / notes:
- If the sanitized sample still contains structured PHI fields (even if anonymized), we should perform a small redaction spike (2–3 days) to validate the redaction pipeline end-to-end. This aligns with Samantha's PHI-safe validation ask.
- Latency target looks achievable on our 4xA10 pool for the pilot, but we need the payload size distribution (median tokens per call) to size batching/CPU headroom.
- Integration: if Flux plans to call the model via client-side JS, we should validate CORS and rate-shaping; server-side proxy is recommended for now.

Optional: propose a 2-day anonymization spike after Week 1 ingestion, deliverable: redaction log and sample audit report. We can include this as a scoped line item in the POC if Flux prefers.

Attachments: redwood-setup-checklist.md (access & network pre-reqs)

Link to shared drive with runbook and telemetry examples: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d-redwood-runbooks

I’ll be available for a short technical pre-kickoff call to walk through the checklist.

Cheers,
Ben
